import numpy as np

# --- helpers to reduce perception noise by averaging several calls ---
def avg_pose(name, n=10):
    ps, qs = [], []
    for _ in range(n):
        p, q = get_object_pose(name)
        ps.append(p); qs.append(q)
    return np.mean(ps, axis=0), qs[0]

def avg_grasp(name, n=10):
    ps, qs = [], []
    for _ in range(n):
        p, q = sample_grasp_pose(name)
        ps.append(p); qs.append(q)
    # keep a consistent orientation: use first quaternion, average only positions
    return np.mean(ps, axis=0), qs[0]

goto_home_joint_position()
open_gripper()

# --- perceive nut center, handle grasp and block ---
nut_center_pos, _ = avg_pose('white hollow center of the brown square nut')
grasp_pos, grasp_quat = avg_grasp('extruded handle of the brown square nut')
block_pos, _ = avg_pose('brown square block')

# rigid offset between the handle grasp point and the nut's hollow center (world frame).
# Since we keep the gripper orientation unchanged while carrying the nut, this offset stays valid.
offset = grasp_pos - nut_center_pos

# --- grasp the nut by its handle ---
goto_pose(grasp_pos, grasp_quat, z_approach=0.10)
close_gripper()

# lift straight up
lift_pos = grasp_pos.copy()
lift_pos[2] += 0.20
goto_pose(lift_pos, grasp_quat)

# --- move so that the nut's hollow center is above the peg ---
target_center = block_pos.copy()
target_center[2] = block_pos[2] + 0.05  # slightly above the block, nut will slide down the peg
place_pos = target_center + offset
place_pos_high = place_pos.copy()
place_pos_high[2] = lift_pos[2]
goto_pose(place_pos_high, grasp_quat)

# insert: descend vertically onto the peg
goto_pose(place_pos, grasp_quat, z_approach=0.12)
open_gripper()

# retreat
goto_pose(place_pos_high, grasp_quat)
goto_home_joint_position()
